result.title: Stand-In Effects and Pooling Amplification: Design-Based Tests of Whether Biological World Models Use Actions
result.comment: 54 pages, 6 figures, 24 tables. Preregistrations: https://doi.org/10.17605/OSF.IO/ZXAR3 (M4) and https://doi.org/10.17605/OSF.IO/QEZBX (M5). Primary category cs.LG: a test for learned action-conditioned models; cross-listed for the statistical method (stat.ME) and the biological application (q-bio.QM)
result.summary: Action-conditioned world models are increasingly trained on data from randomized experiments, and whether their predictions respond to actions is usually checked by replacing or removing the actions and measuring the loss in accuracy. We show that such diagnostics report action effects where there are none: under autocorrelated designs, future actions stand in for history the model does not see, and a better model learns the stand-in better. When the design law is known, a conditional randomization test written as an e-value is valid in finite samples whatever the model, provided the resampler conditions on the full state the design used; resampling from a simpler law reproduces the false effect. We identify a second failure, specific to world models: when many sites share one action sequence (cells in a microscope field, pixels in a frame), the natural pooled score turns small model errors along the action contrast into overwhelming evidence against a true effect. In a pixel world, its median log e-value fell from $-17.3$ to $-6832$ as frames grew from 64 to 4096 pixels, while the oracle's rose. Tempering the score by a design effect estimated on training data changes the bet, not the validity. Our own preregistered analysis of optogenetic ERK experiments failed in exactly this way; a tempered statistic, selected on synthetic data and registered before the data were obtained, then rejected the null on a never-opened field ($E\approx 1.1\times10^{10}$). Every analysis is preregistered, fixed in a dated protocol before it was run, or labelled exploratory, and every reported result is generated from hashed result files.

AI.brief_summary: 论文检验「替换或移除动作再看精度损失」这类诊断能否证明动作条件世界模型真的使用了动作，指出自相关设计下动作会成为未观测历史的替身、多站点共享同一动作序列时池化得分会把微小误差放大为压倒性证据，并提出基于已知设计律的条件随机化 e-value 检验，辅以预注册的光遗传 ERK 实验实例。
AI.relevance_reason: 对 LVR 中「答案是否真的使用 latent 视觉内容」的消融/替换式归因是直接警示：输入自相关与跨 patch、token 的池化可能把微小误差变成虚假证据，其条件重采样检验与「设计效应」处理可供核查。
